name: and.themeMode
label: Theme mode
doc: `auto`, `modern` / `material`, `hololight` (default for existing apps), `legacy`. `auto` and `modern` / `material` opt in to the CSS-generated Android Material 3 theme from `native-themes/android-material/theme.css`. `hololight` is Android Holo Light (what the framework shipped on API 14+ before this refactor). `legacy` loads the pre-Holo Android theme. The legacy alias `cn1.androidTheme` is still accepted, and `and.hololight=true` still maps to `hololight`. The default stays on `hololight` for existing apps until you flip in a future release.

name: android.activity.launchMode
label: Activity launch mode
doc: Allows explicitly setting the `android:launchMode` attribute of the main activity in android. Default is "singleTop," but for some applications you may need to change this behaviour. In particular, apps that are meant to open a file type will need to set this to "singleTask." See https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/activity-element.html[Android docs for the activity element] for more information about the `android:launchMode` attribute.

name: android.appBundle
label: App bundle
doc: Produces an Android App Bundle (.aab) rather than an APK. Required for new Play Store submissions.

name: android.buildToolsVersion
label: Build tools version
doc: Android build-tools version. It also selects the compile SDK, so there is no separate compile-SDK hint.

name: android.captureRecord
label: Capture record
doc: Indicates whether the `RECORD_AUDIO` permission should be requested. Can be `enabled` or any other value to disable this option

name: android.debug
label: Debug
doc: Whether to include the debug version in the build. This hint has NO single default, which is why none is recorded: `AndroidGradleBuilder` reads it with a default of `"false"` under `android.release` and `"true"` otherwise, so a build that selects neither still produces something installable (AndroidGradleBuilder.java:447-451, :530-531).

name: android.disableR8
label: Disable r8
doc: Turns off R8, falling back to the older shrinker. Note that hardening requires R8, so this conflicts with harden.level.

name: android.enableProguard
label: Enable proguard
doc: Boolean true/false defaults to true. Allows disabling the proguard obfuscation even on release builds, notice that this isn't recommended

name: android.gradleDep
label: Gradle dep
doc: Gradle dependency statements to add to the app module, such as implementation 'com.example:lib:1.0'.

name: android.hideStatusBar
label: Hide status bar
doc: Hides the Android status bar.

name: android.installLocation
label: Install location
doc: Maps to android:installLocation manifest entry defaults to auto. Can also be set to internalOnly or preferExternal.

name: android.licenseKey
label: License key
doc: The license key for the Android app, this is required if you use in-app purchase on Android

name: android.min_sdk_version
label: Min sdk version
doc: The least SDK required to run this app, the default value changes based on functionality but can be as low as 7. This corresponds to the XML attribute `android:minSdkVersion`.

name: android.multidex
label: Multidex
doc: Multidex lets an Android binary reference more than 65536 methods. Defaults to TRUE: `AndroidGradleBuilder` reads this hint with a default of `"true"`, so a build that says nothing gets multidex. Set it to false to opt out, which builds a little faster and reinstates the limit.

name: android.newFirebaseMessaging
label: New firebase messaging
doc: Uses the current Firebase Cloud Messaging integration. Requires AndroidX and Gradle 8.13 or newer.

name: android.onDeviceDebug
label: Android
doc: Boolean true/false defaults to false. When `true`, the generated `AndroidManifest.xml` is marked `android:debuggable="true"`, R8/proguard is disabled, and the build is pinned to debug-only (`android.release` is forced off and `android.debug` is forced on) so a stray hint can't ship a release-signed APK that's `debuggable="true"`. Pair with the `cn1:android-on-device-debugging` Maven goal (or the bundled IntelliJ run configs) to install, launch, forward JDWP, and stream logcat through adb. Has no effect on builds that don't carry it -- release builds are unaffected. See the On-Device Debugging (Android) chapter for the full flow.

name: android.proguardKeep
label: Proguard keep
doc: Arguments for the keep option in proguard allowing you to keep a pattern of files for example, `-keep class com.mypackage.ProblemClass { *; }`

name: android.release
label: Release
doc: true/false defaults to true - indicates whether to include the release version in the build

name: android.repositories
label: Repositories
doc: Extra Gradle repositories to resolve dependencies from.

name: android.targetSDKVersion
label: Target sDKVersion
doc: The Android SDK the build compiles against. Unset, the build server uses the highest platform it has installed, so leaving this alone tracks the server rather than pinning a number. Not every target works: the source may have limitations, and not all SDK targets are installed.

name: android.topDependency
label: Top dependency
doc: Statements added to the top-level Gradle build file rather than the app module.

name: android.useAndroidX
label: Use android x
doc: Use Android X instead of support libraries. This will also run a find/replace on all source files to replace support libraries and artifacts with AndroidX equivalents.

name: android.xapplication
label: Xapplication
doc: defaults to an empty string. Allows developers of native Android code to add text within the application block to define things such as widgets, services etc.

name: android.xgradle
label: Xgradle
doc: Arbitrary text spliced into the generated app-module Gradle file.

name: android.xpermissions
label: Xpermissions
doc: more permissions for the Android manifest

name: desktop.adaptToRetina
label: Adapt to retina
doc: Boolean true/false defaults to true. When set to true some values will ve implicitly doubled to deal with retina displays and icons etc. Will use higher DPI's

name: desktop.fullscreen
label: Fullscreen
doc: Starts the desktop build in full-screen mode.

name: desktop.height
label: Height
doc: Height in pixels for the form in desktop builds, will be doubled for retina grade displays. Defaults to 600.

name: desktop.interactiveScrollbars
label: Interactive scrollbars
doc: Enables grab-able, click-to-page desktop scrollbars.

name: desktop.resizable
label: Resizable
doc: Boolean true/false defaults to true. Indicates whether the UI in the desktop build is resizable

name: desktop.titleBar
label: Title bar
doc: How the desktop window is framed: native for the OS title bar and menu bar, custom for an undecorated window with a Codename One drawn title bar, or toolbar for the legacy in-app Toolbar. An unrecognized value falls back to native with a warning.

name: desktop.width
label: Width
doc: Width in pixels for the form in desktop builds, will be doubled for retina grade displays. Defaults to 800.

name: facebook.appId
label: Facebook app id
doc: The application ID for an app that requires native Facebook login integration, this defaults to null which means native Facebook support shouldn't be in the app

name: gcm.sender_id
label: Gcm sender id
doc: The Android/chrome push identifier, see the push section for more details

name: harden.allowUnhardenedLocalBuild
label: Allow unhardened local build
doc: Permits a local or source build to run with hardening requested but not applied. Without it such a build is refused, so a hardened app is never shipped from a target that can't actually harden it.

name: harden.controlFlow
label: Control flow
doc: Overrides control-flow obfuscation independently of harden.level.

name: harden.keep
label: Keep
doc: Keep rules in ProGuard syntax, one per line, for classes that are resolved by name at runtime and so can't be found by the automatic analysis. Same syntax as android.proguardKeep, so existing rules port directly. Rules are separated by newlines only, because a semicolon is legal inside a rule body such as { *; }.

name: harden.level
label: Level
doc: Master switch for app hardening: off, standard, aggressive or paranoid. An unrecognized value fails the build rather than being treated as off.

name: harden.rename
label: Rename
doc: Overrides symbol renaming independently of harden.level.

name: harden.strings
label: Strings
doc: Overrides string obfuscation independently of harden.level: off, constants or all.

name: ios.NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription
label: Bluetooth always usage description
doc: Why the app uses Bluetooth. Supplied automatically when the app references `com.codename1.bluetooth`; set it to say something more specific than the default.

name: ios.NSBluetoothPeripheralUsageDescription
label: Bluetooth peripheral usage description
doc: The pre-iOS 13 spelling of the Bluetooth usage description, supplied and overridable on the same terms.

name: ios.NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription
label: Calendars full access usage description
doc: The text iOS shows when the app first asks for the calendars full access. It becomes the `NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription` key in `Info.plist`. The App Store rejects an app that touches this resource without one.

name: ios.NSCalendarsUsageDescription
label: Calendars usage description
doc: The text iOS shows when the app first asks for the calendars. It becomes the `NSCalendarsUsageDescription` key in `Info.plist`. The App Store rejects an app that touches this resource without one.

name: ios.NSCalendarsWriteOnlyAccessUsageDescription
label: Calendars write only access usage description
doc: The text iOS shows when the app first asks for the calendars write only access. It becomes the `NSCalendarsWriteOnlyAccessUsageDescription` key in `Info.plist`. The App Store rejects an app that touches this resource without one.

name: ios.NSCameraUsageDescription
label: Camera usage description
doc: The text iOS shows when the app first asks for the camera. It becomes the `NSCameraUsageDescription` key in `Info.plist`. The App Store rejects an app that touches this resource without one.

name: ios.NSHealthShareUsageDescription
label: Health share usage description
doc: The text iOS shows when the app first asks for the health share. It becomes the `NSHealthShareUsageDescription` key in `Info.plist`. The App Store rejects an app that touches this resource without one.

name: ios.NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription
label: Health update usage description
doc: The text iOS shows when the app first asks for the health update. It becomes the `NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription` key in `Info.plist`. The App Store rejects an app that touches this resource without one.

name: ios.NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription
label: Local network usage description
doc: The text iOS shows when the app first asks for the local network. It becomes the `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription` key in `Info.plist`. The App Store rejects an app that touches this resource without one.

name: ios.NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription
label: Location always and when in use usage description
doc: The text iOS shows when the app first asks for the location always and when in use. It becomes the `NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescription` key in `Info.plist`. The App Store rejects an app that touches this resource without one.

name: ios.NSLocationAlwaysUsageDescription
label: Location always usage description
doc: The text iOS shows when the app first asks for the location always. It becomes the `NSLocationAlwaysUsageDescription` key in `Info.plist`. The App Store rejects an app that touches this resource without one.

name: ios.NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription
label: Location when in use usage description
doc: The text iOS shows when the app first asks for the location when in use. It becomes the `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription` key in `Info.plist`. The App Store rejects an app that touches this resource without one.

name: ios.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription
label: Microphone usage description
doc: The text iOS shows when the app first asks for the microphone. It becomes the `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` key in `Info.plist`. The App Store rejects an app that touches this resource without one.

name: ios.NSNearbyInteractionAllowOnceUsageDescription
label: Nearby interaction allow once usage description
doc: The pre-iOS 16 spelling of the nearby-interaction usage description, supplied automatically when the app references the nearby APIs.

name: ios.NSNearbyInteractionUsageDescription
label: Nearby interaction usage description
doc: Why the app measures distance and direction to nearby devices. Supplied automatically when the app references the nearby APIs; set it to say something more specific than the default.

name: ios.NSRemindersFullAccessUsageDescription
label: Reminders full access usage description
doc: The text iOS shows when the app first asks for the reminders full access. It becomes the `NSRemindersFullAccessUsageDescription` key in `Info.plist`. The App Store rejects an app that touches this resource without one.

name: ios.NSRemindersUsageDescription
label: Reminders usage description
doc: The text iOS shows when the app first asks for the reminders. It becomes the `NSRemindersUsageDescription` key in `Info.plist`. The App Store rejects an app that touches this resource without one.

name: ios.NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription
label: Speech recognition usage description
doc: Why the app sends speech for recognition. Supplied automatically when the app references the speech APIs; set it to say something more specific.

name: ios.add_libs
label: Add libs
doc: A semicolon separated list of libraries that should be linked to the app to build it

name: ios.applicationQueriesSchemes
label: Application queries schemes
doc: Comma separated list of url schemes that `canExecute` will respect on iOS. If the url scheme isn't mentioned here `canExecute` will return false starting with iOS 9. Notice that this collides with `ios.plistInject` when used with the `<key>LSApplicationQueriesSchemes</key>...` value so you should use one or the other. For example, to enable `canExecute` for a url like `myurl://xys` you can use: `myurl,myotherurl`

name: ios.beforeFinishLaunching
label: Before finish launching
doc: Objective-C code that can be injected into the iOS app delegate at the top of the body of the didFinishLaunchingWithOptions callback method

name: ios.bundleVersion
label: Bundle version
doc: Indicates the version number of the bundle, this is useful if you want to create a minor version number change for the beta testing support

name: ios.dependencyManager
label: Dependency manager
doc: Which native dependency manager to use: auto picks one from whichever of ios.pods and ios.spm.packages is set, and cocoapods, spm or both require the matching hint to be set. An unrecognized value fails the build.

name: ios.deployment_target
label: Deployment target
doc: Minimum iOS version the build targets. Set it to the lowest iOS you actually support; a higher value excludes older devices from the App Store listing.

name: ios.glAppDelegateHeader
label: Gl app delegate header
doc: Objective-C code that can be injected into the iOS app delegate at the top of the file. For example, if you need to include headers or make special imports for other injected code

name: ios.includePush
label: Include push
doc: true/false (defaults to false). Whether to include the push capabilities in the iOS build. Notice that the IDE plugin has an "Include Push" check box you *should* use under the iOS section.

name: ios.interface_orientation
label: Interface orientation
doc: UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait by default. Indicates the orientation, one or more of (separated by colon :): `UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait`, `UIInterfaceOrientationPortraitUpsideDown`, `UIInterfaceOrientationLandscapeLeft`, `UIInterfaceOrientationLandscapeRight`. Notice that the IDE plugin has an "Interface Orientation" combo box you *should* use under the iOS section.

name: ios.minDeploymentTarget
label: Min deployment target
doc: The null and empty-string reads of this hint are presence checks; 6.0 is the substantive default (IPhoneBuilder.java:4671).

name: ios.newStorageLocation
label: New storage location
doc: Stores app files under the documents directory rather than caches, which is the location Apple recommends but which may break compatibility with an app that already shipped. Defaults to TRUE: `IPhoneBuilder` reads this hint with a default of `"true"`, so a build that says nothing gets it. Described in https://github.com/codenameone/CodenameOne/issues/1480[this issue]

name: ios.objC
label: Obj c
doc: Added the `-ObjC` compile flag to the project files which some native libraries require

name: ios.onDeviceDebug
label: Ios
doc: Boolean true/false defaults to false. When `true`, the iOS build links a small JDWP listener thread (`cn1_debugger`) into the binary and the ParparVM translator emits source-line and locals metadata so a desktop proxy can serve the running app to any JDWP-speaking debugger. Has no effect on release builds. See the On-Device Debugging (iOS) chapter for the full flow.

name: ios.onDeviceDebug.proxyHost
label: Ios proxy host
doc: Hostname or IP address the device-side listener dials to reach the desktop proxy. Default `127.0.0.1` (correct for the native iOS simulator). For a physical device, set this to the developer laptop's LAN IP. Has no effect unless `ios.onDeviceDebug=true`.

name: ios.onDeviceDebug.proxyPort
label: Ios proxy port
doc: TCP port on `ios.onDeviceDebug.proxyHost` where the proxy is listening for the device. Default `55333`. Has no effect unless `ios.onDeviceDebug=true`.

name: ios.onDeviceDebug.waitForAttach
label: Ios wait for attach
doc: Boolean true/false defaults to false. When `true`, the app blocks at startup until the proxy connects and the IDE tells the VM to continue. Useful when the breakpoint to investigate fires during app boot. Has no effect unless `ios.onDeviceDebug=true`.

name: ios.plistInject
label: Plist inject
doc: entries to inject into the iOS plist file during build.

name: ios.pods
label: Pods
doc: A comma separated list of https://cocoapods.org/[Cocoa Pods] that should be linked to the app to build it. For example, `AFNetworking ~> 2.6, ORStackView ~> 3.0, SwiftyJSON ~> 2.3`

name: ios.pods.platform
label: Pods platform
doc: Sets the Cocoapods 'platform' for the Cocoapods. Some Cocoapods require a minimum platform level. For example, `ios.pods.platform=7.0`.

name: ios.pods.sources
label: Pods sources
doc: Extra CocoaPods spec repositories to search, in addition to the default trunk.

name: ios.prerendered_icon
label: Prerendered icon
doc: true/false defaults to false. The iOS build process adapts the submitted icon for iOS conventions (adding an overlay) that might not be appropriate on some icons. Setting this to true leaves the icon unchanged (only scaled).

name: ios.project_type
label: Project type
doc: one of ios, ipad, iphone (defaults to ios). Indicates whether the resulting binary is targeted to the iphone only or ipad only. Notice that the IDE plugin has a "Project Type" combo box you *should* use under the iOS section.

name: ios.spm.packages
label: Spm packages
doc: Swift Package Manager packages to link, one per entry, each written as identity|url|requirement.

name: ios.teamId
label: Team id
doc: Specifies the team ID associated with the iOS provisioning profile and certificate. Use `ios.debug.teamId` and `ios.release.teamId` to specify different team IDs for debug and release builds respectively.

name: ios.themeMode
label: Theme mode
doc: `auto` (default), `modern`, `ios7`, `legacy`. `auto` (unset) keeps the existing iOS 7 flat theme so pre-refactor screenshot goldens and apps see no behavior change. `modern` / `liquid` opts in to the CSS-generated iOS Modern (liquid-glass) theme shipped from `native-themes/ios-modern/theme.css`. `ios7` / `flat` is the same as `auto` - pre-liquid iOS 7 flat theme; `legacy` / `iphone` loads the pre-iOS 7 iPhone theme. The `auto` -> modern flip is planned for a future release.

name: ios.uiscene
label: Uiscene
doc: true/false (defaults to true). Enables iOS UIScene lifecycle support. UIScene lets iOS manage one or more app UI sessions independently, improving lifecycle handling in modern iOS versions. Apple has indicated UIScene will be required starting with iOS 27, so this is now on by default; set the flag to `false` only if you need to temporarily fall back to the legacy `UIApplicationDelegate` lifecycle.

name: ios.urlScheme
label: Url scheme
doc: Allows intercepting a URL call using the syntax `<string>urlPrefix<string>`

name: nativeTheme
label: Native theme
doc: `modern`, `legacy`, `custom` (default unset). Cross-platform override that sets both `ios.themeMode` and `and.themeMode` together when those aren't set explicitly. `modern` = liquid glass + Material 3, `legacy` = iOS 7 flat + Holo Light, `custom` disables the framework native theme entirely. The legacy alias `cn1.nativeTheme` is still accepted.

name: noExtraResources
label: No extra resources
doc: true/false (defaults to false). Blocks codename one from injecting its own resources when set to true, the only effect this has is in slightly reducing archive size. This might have adverse effects on some features of Codename One so it isn't recommended.
